name: Monport GPro Vision 60W MOPA
tagline: Split MOPA fiber with 16 MP camera and autofocus: the colour-marking entry of the GPro Vision line
tldr: The GPro Vision 60W MOPA adds Monport's 16 MP positioning camera and autofocus to a 60W MOPA source with a 175 × 175 mm field. MOPA pulse control opens colour marking on stainless steel and titanium and cleaner marks on plastics; Monport rates it for brass up to 2.5 mm thick. $5,299 on Monport's store in October 2026, listed for mid-October shipping. The line launched in June 2026; no independent review yet.
mainObjective: Colour marking and fine metal engraving with camera placement

priceRange.note: Official Monport store, Oct 2026: $5,299 machine only, $5,499 with LightBurn Pro, listed for mid-October shipping

engraveExample.description: Filled logo on stainless steel plate

cutExample.description: Not a sheet cutter: thin metal only, in many passes

cut: Brass up to 2.5 mm (Monport figure, many passes)
cannot: Clear glass or acrylic marking (needs UV or CO₂)
Parts larger than the 175 × 175 mm field without repositioning

pros: MOPA source: controlled colour on stainless steel and titanium, cleaner marks on plastics and anodized aluminum
16 MP camera and autofocus for placing artwork on irregular parts and laying out batches
Rated by Monport to cut brass up to 2.5 mm thick, in many passes
cons: About $600 more than Monport's GT MOPA at the same power, which has autofocus but no camera
175 × 175 mm field, smaller than the entry tier's
Listed for mid-October shipping in October 2026, and no independent review of the line yet

faq.question: How much does the camera cost over a GT 60W MOPA?
faq.answer: About $600: the GPro Vision 60W MOPA is $5,299 on Monport's store in October 2026, the GT 60W MOPA with autofocus $4,699.99. Both use a 60W MOPA source and a 175 × 175 mm field; the GPro Vision adds the 16 MP camera for visual placement, batch layouts and Monport's conveyor accessory.

faq.question: Is the GPro Vision 60W MOPA in stock?
faq.answer: In October 2026 Monport listed the 60W MOPA with a mid-October shipping note, so expect a short wait; the 50W and 100W tiers were shown without a delay. Check the note next to the power option before ordering.

faq.question: 60W or 100W MOPA?
faq.answer: The 60W ($5,299) covers colour marking, black marking, plastics and light engraving. The 100W ($6,919.99) shares the field and camera but removes material faster, which matters for deep relief, 3D embossing and cutting thin sheet. Choose by depth and throughput, not by colour: both do colour.

standoutFeatures.title: Colour marking with camera placement
standoutFeatures.body: MOPA pulse control for oxide colours on stainless steel and titanium, combined with a 16 MP camera to position artwork on finished parts.

standoutFeatures.title: Thin-metal cutting
standoutFeatures.body: Monport rates this tier for brass up to 2.5 mm thick. Expect many passes: it is a marking laser that can cut small parts, not a sheet cutter.

beginnerNotes: This profile is the 60W MOPA tier of the GPro Vision, the least expensive one with controlled colour marking. Compare the other tiers via the chips if you need a wider field or more depth.
proTips: Build colour test grids on your own alloy before quoting colour jobs: results depend on surface finish, speed and frequency. Recalibrate the camera after changing the lens.

editorialDepth.advantages: The 60W MOPA is the balanced tier of the GPro Vision: colour and fine marking on metals and plastics, a camera that speeds up placement on finished goods, and enough power for light engraving and small brass cut-outs.
editorialDepth.limitations: It costs noticeably more than the camera-less GT equivalent, the field is 175 × 175 mm, and the open design needs an enclosure or strict eye protection. Specs are Monport's until independent tests arrive.
